chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, who said:

I sent a question to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with Ibrahim ibn Maymun, saying: Ask him about a man who urinates and a drop of his urine strikes his thigh, the size of a pinpoint, and he prays and then remembers afterward that he did not wash it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must wash it and repeat his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I missed washing a small drop of urine after finishing my prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for minor impurity (najāsah khafīfah) on the body, specifically urine on the thigh. It establishes that while the prayer is not invalidated by the oversight, the individual must wash the affected area and repeat the prayer upon remembering, distinguishing this from cases where the impurity is forgotten until after the prayer concludes. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on both the validity (ṣiḥḥah) and perfection (kamāl) of worship, ensuring ritual purity is maintained even in minor oversights.
